author: mark
text:
Hard rule clarification (2026-04-27): request.json and response.json
have NO runtime integration in the harness — ever. They are
write-only diagnostic artifacts. The frontend may read them (user
inspection); the harness must not.

Concretely:
- Step-loop messages history: assembled in-memory within one
  process; never reconstructed by reading prior response.json.
- Replay / retry within a step: rebuilds the request by re-running
  the context assembler against the snapshot commit's tree, never
  by reading request.json.
- Resume across processes: scoped to workflow-event boundaries
  (ARCH §1 #4, §603), not mid-conversation. A crashed process
  loses any in-flight step's wire state — accepted, since the
  diagnostic record is sufficient for human triage.
- Tool input/output records (tools/<tool-id>/{input,output}.json)
  are NOT covered by this rule — tool outputs are nondeterministic
  and the harness must read output.json to assemble the next
  step's tool_result blocks. They share the relocation path
  (out-of-worktree) but keep their runtime read.

P1 (ARCH amendment) must pin this rule explicitly so future code
can't accidentally regress. P2 onward must structurally enforce it
via path location + verified absence of read sites.
